body:
<!--
Title (above): please place [branch_name] at the beginning if you are targeting a branch other than master. *Do not target stable*.
It is recommended to use conventional commit format, see conventionalcommits.org, but not required.
-->
## Description
Follow-on to PR #5700, specifically [this comment](https://github.com/pybind/pybind11/pull/5700#issuecomment-2915297794).
________

This PR addresses fragile RTTI-based operations across dynamic shared object (DSO) boundaries, which commonly cause failures on macOS (due to libc++'s RTTI implementation). This is achieved by capturing required RTTI-dependent behavior in the DSO that defines the type, and using only function pointers elsewhere.

**The three main changes:**

* **Cross-DSO-safe `get_guarded_delete`**

    The `pybind11::detail::type_info` struct now stores a function pointer (`get_guarded_delete`) for retrieving the `guarded_delete` from a `shared_ptr<void>`.

    This avoids direct use of `std::get_deleter<T>` across DSOs, where RTTI comparisons may fail.

* **Cross-DSO-safe `get_trampoline_self_life_support`**

    Similarly, `pybind11::detail::type_info` now includes a `get_trampoline_self_life_support` function pointer.

    The lambda is defined in the same DSO that instantiates `class_`, where the alias type (aka trampoline) is known and the cast is valid.

    This replaces `dynamic_cast<trampoline_self_life_support *>(...)` with a safer, cross-DSO-compatible mechanism.

* **Resilient handling of `std::unique_ptr` deleters in `struct smart_holder`**

    RTTI comparisons are made tolerant to DSO boundaries by comparing `typeid(...).name()` as a fallback.

    The boolean `vptr_is_using_std_default_delete` tracks whether `std::default_delete<T>` (or its `const` variant) was used.

    This allows correct ownership transfer and deletion logic even when RTTI identity fails across DSOs.

**Other details:**

* This PR removes `PYBIND11_EXPORT_GUARDED_DELETE` that was introduced as a stop-gap with PR #5700.

* `PYBIND11_INTERNALS_VERSION` was bumped from `10` to `11` to reflect these ABI-relevant changes.

* All uses of `std::get_deleter<guarded_delete>` have been replaced by `type_info->get_memory_guarded_delete(...)`.

* Unit tests in `smart_holder_poc_test.cpp` and elsewhere were updated to pass in `get_guarded_delete` explicitly where required.

These changes make trampoline support and smart_holder-based ownership transfer robust on macOS and other environments with strict DSO isolation.
________

See also: [claude.ai full review](https://claude.ai/share/a9f268ae-8bd1-4b59-977a-7ba5dbc7f786)

For completeness: [Extremely long ChatGPT conversation](https://chatgpt.com/share/684f3583-15e4-8008-b89d-9aedc0787ccb) related to the work on this PR.

## Suggested changelog entry:

<!-- Fill in the block below with the expected entry. Delete if no entry needed;

* Eliminate cross-DSO RTTI reliance from `trampoline_self_life_support` functionality, `smart_holder` deleter detection, and other `smart_holder` bookkeeping. Resolves platform-specific issues on macOS related to cross-DSO `dynamic_cast` and `typeid` mismatches.

author: zen0x7
body:
This is a "security concern". My advice is simple, throttr SDK must be used on internal networks, i mean, not exposed.

I add the Sonar related comment:

```
Most of the regular expression engines use backtracking to try all possible execution paths of the regular expression when evaluating an input, in some cases it can cause performance issues, called catastrophic backtracking situations. In the worst case, the complexity of the regular expression is exponential in the size of the input, this means that a small carefully-crafted input (like 20 chars) can trigger catastrophic backtracking and cause a denial of service of the application. Super-linear regex complexity can lead to the same impact too with, in this case, a large carefully-crafted input (thousands chars).

This rule determines the runtime complexity of a regular expression and informs you if it is not linear. 
```

This code will be executed to remove zeroes of instance version. (over fixed 16 bytes).

If you think about, this will be executed on `throttr` response parse context. Which is, again, fixed and static protocol. There are no reason to believe in this issue.

author: bioye
body:
# 🚀 Complete Authentication System Implementation

## **Overview**
This PR implements the complete authentication system for the Fashion App, enabling user registration, OTP verification, and login flows for both shoppers and vendors. The system now supports role-based authentication with proper token management and error handling.

## **✅ Features Implemented**

### **🔐 Authentication Core**
- **Fixed authService Architecture**: Resolved import/export patterns by exporting class instance instead of constructor
- **API Endpoint Resolution**: Removed duplicate `/api` path prefixes causing 404 errors
- **JWT Token Management**: Implemented userId extraction from registration tokens for OTP verification
- **Conditional Authentication**: Added storeName handling for vendor-specific login requirements

### **👥 User Registration & Verification**
- **Shopper Flow**: Complete registration → OTP verification → login → dashboard
- **Vendor Flow**: Complete registration → OTP verification → login → dashboard (with storeName)
- **OTP System**: Rate-limited resend functionality with 30-second cooldown
- **Session Management**: Proper cleanup of verification data after successful completion

### **🔑 Login System**
- **Multi-Role Support**: Handles shopper, vendor, and admin authentication
- **Error Handling**: Status-specific error messages (400, 401, 403, 409, 500)
- **Token Storage**: Consistent localStorage management across all user types
- **Navigation**: Role-based redirection after successful authentication

### **🛡️ Security & Validation**
- **Input Validation**: Client-side validation before API calls
- **Password Confirmation**: Repeat password validation for registration
- **Terms Acceptance**: Required agreement to terms and privacy policy
- **Error Recovery**: Graceful handling of network and server errors

## **🧪 Testing Status**

### **✅ Working Flows**
- **Shopper Registration**: Email → OTP → Verification → Login → Dashboard ✅
- **Vendor Registration**: Email + StoreName → OTP → Verification → Login → Dashboard ✅
- **Shopper Login**: Email + Password → Dashboard ✅
- **Vendor Login**: Email + StoreName + Password → Dashboard ✅

### **🔄 In Progress**
- **Admin Login**: Foundation ready, needs dashboard integration
- **Password Reset**: API methods implemented, UI integration pending

## **🔧 Technical Implementation**

### **Backend Integration**
```javascript
// Conditional storeName handling for vendor authentication
const requestBody = {
  identifier: credentials.identifier || credentials.email,
  password: credentials.password,
  role: credentials.role || 'shopper',
  ...(credentials.storeName && { storeName: credentials.storeName })
};
```

### **JWT Token Processing**
```javascript
// Extract userId from JWT for OTP verification
extractUserIdFromToken(token) {
  const payload = JSON.parse(atob(token.split('.')[1]));
  return payload.userId || payload.id || payload.sub || null;
}
```

### **Error Handling Strategy**
```javascript
// Status-specific error messages
if (error.status === 400) {
  setError('Please fill in all required fields correctly.');
} else if (error.status === 409) {
  setError('This email is already registered. Please use a different email.');
}
```

## **🚨 Temporary Solutions**

### **StoreName Requirement**
- **Issue**: Backend currently requires storeName for vendor login
- **Solution**: Conditional inclusion via spread operator
- **Rollback Plan**: Remove storeName logic when backend API updated
- **Marker**: `🚨 TEMPORARY` comments in code

## **🎯 Next Sprint Priorities**

### **1. Vendor Dashboard Implementation**
- Create vendor-specific dashboard components
- Implement role-based routing (`/vendor/dashboard`)
- Add vendor navigation sidebar matching design specs

### **2. Admin Approval Workflow**
- Add vendor status field (pending/approved/rejected)
- Create admin vendor management dashboard
- Implement email notifications for status changes
- Add vendor pending approval UI states

### **3. Admin Login Completion**
- Fix adminLogin API integration
- Create admin dashboard components
- Implement admin-specific navigation

## **📦 Files Changed**

### **Core Services**
- `src/services/authService.js` - Complete authentication service with all methods
- `src/contexts/AuthContext.jsx` - Updated context with logout functionality

### **UI Components**
- `src/components/Auth-Designer/RegisterForm.jsx` - Shopper registration with OTP flow
- `src/components/Auth-Designer/VendorRegisterForm.jsx` - Vendor registration with storeName
- `src/components/Auth-Designer/LoginForm.jsx` - Shopper login with role-based navigation
- `src/components/Auth-Designer/VendorLoginForm.jsx` - Vendor login with storeName validation
- `src/components/Auth-Designer/AdminLoginForm.jsx` - Admin login foundation
- `src/components/Auth-Designer/OTPInput.jsx` - Enhanced OTP verification with rate limiting

### **Configuration**
- `.vscode/settings.json` - Enhanced copilot settings with git push requirements

## **🔗 API Endpoints Used**

- `POST /auth/register` - User registration ✅
- `POST /auth/verify-otp` - Email verification ✅
- `POST /auth/resend-otp` - Resend verification code ✅
- `POST /auth/login` - User authentication ✅
- `POST /admin/login` - Admin authentication 🔄

## **🎓 Learning Outcomes**

### **React Patterns Implemented**
- **Default Exports**: Class instance exports for immediate method availability
- **Conditional Spread**: Dynamic object properties for flexible API payloads
- **Error Boundaries**: Graceful error handling with user-friendly messages
- **Session Management**: Proper cleanup of temporary data after workflows
- **Form Validation**: Client-side validation before API calls

### **Authentication Architecture**
- **JWT Token Processing**: Manual token parsing for userId extraction
- **Role-Based Routing**: Different navigation paths based on user type
- **State Management**: Consistent user state across components
- **API Integration**: Proper error handling and response processing

## **🔍 Review Focus Areas**

1. **Security**: Token storage and user data handling
2. **Error Handling**: All error scenarios covered with user-friendly messages
3. **User Experience**: Smooth registration/login flows with proper feedback
4. **Code Quality**: Consistent patterns and proper React component structure
5. **API Integration**: Correct endpoint usage and response handling

## **🚀 Deployment Ready**

This PR establishes the foundation authentication system that enables:
- Complete user onboarding for both shoppers and vendors
- Secure token-based authentication
- Role-based access control
- Proper error handling and user feedback

The system is ready for production deployment and sets up the foundation for the next phase of vendor dashboard and admin approval workflows.

author: edilvolima
body:
This commit addresses issues in the `k8s-tools-cluster` Ansible role:
- Modified `tasks/deploy-rke.yml` to execute the `rke up` command from the `/vagrant` directory. This ensures that relative SSH key paths defined in `cluster.yml` (generated from the template) are correctly resolved, fixing a common RKE deployment failure point in Vagrant environments.
- Uncommented and set `cluster_name: k8s-tools` in the `templates/cluster.yml.j2` for clarity and explicitness in the RKE configuration.

Additionally, this commit introduces:
- `CHANGELOG.md`: A new changelog file to track project modifications. It has been initialized with details of the current fixes and additions.
- `play_verify_k8s-tools_cluster.yml`: A new Ansible playbook designed for basic post-deployment verification of the `k8s-tools` cluster. This playbook checks for the kubeconfig file, attempts to retrieve node status using `kubectl get nodes`, and asserts that nodes are in a 'Ready' state.

The `jules-dev` branch was created from `main` and includes these updates.

## Summary by Sourcery

Fix the k8s-tools-cluster role to resolve RKE deployment failures by running `rke up` from the correct directory and explicitly setting the cluster name, and introduce a changelog plus an Ansible playbook for post-deployment cluster verification.

New Features:
- Add `play_verify_k8s-tools_cluster.yml` playbook to verify kubeconfig presence, node status retrieval, and node readiness.

Bug Fixes:
- Run the RKE deployment task from `/vagrant` to resolve relative SSH key path issues.
- Uncomment and set `cluster_name: k8s-tools` in the cluster template for explicit naming.

Documentation:
- Introduce `CHANGELOG.md` following the Keep a Changelog format.

author: jackbuehner
body:
## Background and change

macOS, iOS, iPadOS, and Android all support the [rdp URI scheme](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows-server/remote/remote-desktop-services/remote-desktop-uri#legacy-rdp-uri-scheme). It allows you to launch the remote desktop client and automatically connect to a specific desktop or RemoteApp. Additioanlly, Windows clients can add support via apps like the proof-of-concept app I made, [RDP Protocol Handler](https://github.com/jackbuehner/rdp-protocol-handler/tree/main/dist), which converts the URI to an RDP file and launches it.

This PR adds support for launching RemoteApps and desktops via the rdp URI scheme. Here's how it works when you try to launch an app or desktop from the RAWeb web app:
1. Click on an app or desktop.
2. A prompt to select the connection method appears. Currently supported methods are RDP files and rdp://.
![image](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/81d0db32-9149-469e-ad2b-c8bd34ed8672)
3. Click **Always** or **Just once**, or double click a method. If you choose **Always**, this prompt will be skipped in the future. You can force the prompt to appears with the **Connect with...** context menu option for apps and desktops. If you choose **Just once**, the prompt will be shown next time. If you double click, the prompt will not change your launch preference.
4. If the RemoteApp is available on multiple terminal servers, another prompt to choose the terminal server will appear. This is already part of RAWeb.
5. If you choose the RDP file option, the file will be downloaded. If you choose the rdp:// option, your browser will attempt to open the rdp:// URI.
   - On your first launch with the rdp:// option, if you are on Windows, an additional prompt to download the [Remote Desktop Protocol Handler](https://apps.microsoft.com/detail/9N1192WSCHV9?hl=en-us&gl=US&ocid=pdpshare) app from the Microsoft Store will appear. Windows does not have built-in support for rdp://, but this app adds support. It can also be installed with `winget install "RDP Protocol Handler" --source msstore`.
![image](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/a33f83c0-7e89-4442-918a-303325044ecc)
   - On macOS, iOS, or iPadOS, you will be prompted to download Windows App from the App Store.

## Caveats

- If an RDP file is signed, the option to launch via rdp:// will be hidden. RAWeb is currently unable to parse signed RDP files, which means it cannot construct an rdp:// URI.
- The Android remote desktop client requires rdp:// URIs to not have URL-encoded values (e.g., `remoteapplicationname=s:Windows Explorer` instead of `remoteapplicationname=s%3AWindows%20Explorer`). Because this makes URLs invalid, it is not possible to launch non-url-encoded URLs/URIs in browsers. Because of this limitation, RAWeb will not present the option to launch via rdp:// when the detected OS is Android.
- There are no prompts to download apps on Linux. Users on Linux are expected to ensure they have an app that supports opening rdp:// URIs and then launch RemoteApps or desktops.

## Install this pre-release branch

1. **Open PowerShell as an administrator**
   Press the Windows key + X, then select PowerShell (Administrator) or Terminal (Administrator).

2. **Copy and paste the code below, then press enter.**

 ```
irm https://github.com/jackbuehner/raweb/releases/download/v2025.06.15.0/install.ps1 | iex
```

---

Tested operating systems:

- [x] Windows - chromium
- [x] Windows - gecko
- [x] Android - chromium
- [x] iPadOS - webkit
- [x] macOS - webkit

Resolves #67
Resolves #15

author: kelemen
body:
As is now, we can only set a global `TempFileCreationStrategy` which assumes that all documents within the same process has the same security profile (and quota) which may or may not be the case. Currently it is not possible to workaround this limitation in a multithreaded application.

This PR intends to fix this issue by allowing to set a `TempFileCreationStrategy` for `SXSSFWorkbook` and `ZipPackage` instances.

Implementation notes:

- I have not deleted the `BinaryRC4Encryptor.BinaryRC4CipherOutputStream(DirectoryNode)` constructor because it is protected and in theory might be used (though given that other implementations have the counterparts of this class private, I'm guessing this visibility is unintended).
- When adjusting the `OPCPackage.open` methods (to avoid duplicating logic), I'm relying on a new `OPCPackageOpener` class. However, strictly speaking my implementation is not 100% backward compatible (can be adjusted of course if needed), because the new `OPCPackageOpener` immediately throws NPE when it receives null `PackageAccess` or `OPCComplianceFlags`, while the original implementation does not. Rather, the original implementation will simply store the nulls, and will (likely) throw an exception on first use. Should I adjust my changes to be 100% backward compatible, or is this an acceptable risk for this project?
- Not directly related to this PR, but while making the adjustments, I have noticed that `DefaultTempFileCreationStrategy` is buggy (at least I doubt its behavior is intended): When it detects that the temporary directory does not exist, then it will reset the directory to what is in `java.io.tmpdir` even if a different directory was specified in the constructor. I'm mentioning this only, because this issue can be a security risk (if someone changed the tmp dir due to security reasons), and this PR might make this issue more visible.

body:
## Summary
Implements the Universal Dictation feature as defined in the PRD, enabling users to dictate text into any input field or textarea on any website using Say, Pi's high-quality Whisper-powered transcription.

### Key Features Implemented
- **Universal Voice Input**: Voice-to-text in any text field, textarea, or contenteditable element
- **Real-time Streaming**: Text appears as you speak with low latency using existing Say, Pi architecture
- **Target Switching**: Seamlessly switch between input fields while dictating
- **Manual Edit Preservation**: Users can manually edit dictated text and resume dictation while preserving their changes
- **Context Menu Integration**: Right-click to start dictation in any supported field
- **Visual Feedback**: Floating dictation buttons with state-aware icons and placeholder text
- **Transcription Isolation**: Separate transcription tracking per input field

### Technical Architecture
- **DictationMachine**: New XState finite state machine managing dictation workflow
- **UniversalDictationModule**: Content script managing DOM decoration and user interactions
- **Target Isolation**: Smart transcription tracking that prevents cross-contamination between fields
- **Audio Pipeline Integration**: Reuses existing VAD, audio processing, and transcription infrastructure

### Major Components Added
- `src/state-machines/DictationMachine.ts` (1,134 lines) - Core dictation state machine
- `src/UniversalDictationModule.ts` (1,025 lines) - DOM management and UI interactions
- `src/chatbots/Web.ts` (55 lines) - Web-specific chatbot implementation
- Comprehensive test coverage with 12 test suites covering state transitions, target switching, and manual edit handling

### Manual Edit Innovation
One of the most sophisticated features allows users to:
1. Dictate text into a field: "Hello, World\!"
2. Manually edit the text: "Hello, Earth\!"
3. Resume dictation and the system intelligently updates its transcription records to preserve the manual edits
4. Continue dictating while maintaining edit history

### Test Coverage
- **DictationMachine**: 8 manual edit handling tests + comprehensive state machine tests
- **UniversalDictationModule**: 4 manual edit detection tests + DOM interaction tests
- **Target Switching**: Complex scenarios with multiple simultaneous transcriptions
- **Edge Cases**: Content mismatch protection, provisional target handling, cross-target isolation

### Browser Compatibility
- Chrome/Chromium: Full support with manifest v3
- Firefox: Compatible with existing Firefox-specific adaptations
- ~~All major websites: Tested on various form implementations~~

### Performance Considerations
- Lazy initialization: Only loads on pages with compatible form fields
- Lightweight bootstrap: Minimal impact on page load times
- Efficient DOM observation: Smart mutation tracking for dynamic content
- Memory management: Proper cleanup of event listeners and state machines

This commit introduces a root-level __init__.py file. This file is essential for ComfyUI to discover and load custom nodes located in subdirectories.

The __init__.py imports NODE_CLASS_MAPPINGS and
NODE_DISPLAY_NAME_MAPPINGS from:

- ClearGpuMemoryCacheNode

It then aggregates these mappings and exports them, allowing ComfyUI to register all included custom nodes. Error handling for imports has been added to prevent issues if a node directory is missing.

author: copilot
body:
This PR implements Step 5 of the decoupling plan by separating the audio pipeline into clear, minimal stages with well-defined interfaces and queue-based communication.

## 🏗️ Architecture Changes

The monolithic audio processing has been refactored into three distinct pipeline stages:

1. **AudioCaptureStage** - Captures audio using `AudioInputSource` interface
2. **AudioBufferingStage** - Buffers audio chunks before processing  
3. **RecognitionStage** - Performs recognition using `VoiceRecognitionSource` interface

```python
# Before: Monolithic processing in VoiceTyping.voice_typing_loop()
with sd.RawInputStream(callback=self.audio_callback):
    while True:
        data = self.state_ref.q.get()
        buffer.append(data)
        self.audio_processor.process_buffer(buffer)

# After: Decoupled pipeline stages
coordinator = AudioPipelineCoordinator(audio_input, recognition_source, callback)
await coordinator.start_pipeline()  # Stages communicate via async queues
```

## 🔧 Implementation Details

### Pipeline Interfaces
- **`AudioPipelineStage`** - Abstract base for all pipeline stages
- **`PipelineCoordinator`** - Manages pipeline execution and inter-stage communication

### Concrete Implementations
- **`AudioPipelineCoordinator`** - Orchestrates all stages with async queues
- **`PipelineVoiceTyping`** - Drop-in replacement using pipeline architecture
- **`SoundDeviceAudioInput`** - Concrete audio input implementation

### Queue-Based Communication
- Async queues provide loose coupling between stages
- Configurable queue sizes and buffer management
- Non-blocking data flow prevents bottlenecks

## ✅ Testing & Validation

### Comprehensive Test Suite
- **Individual stage tests** - Each stage tested in isolation with mocks
- **End-to-end pipeline test** - Full coordinator functionality validated
- **Integration tests** - Pipeline integrates with existing system components
- **Demo script** - Shows real data flowing through all stages

```python
# Example: Testing individual stages in isolation
@pytest.mark.asyncio
async def test_audio_capture_stage():
    mock_audio = MockAudioInput()
    stage = AudioCaptureStage(mock_audio)
    output_queue = asyncio.Queue()
    stage.set_output_queue(output_queue)
    
    await stage.start()
    mock_audio.simulate_audio_chunk(b'test_data')
    
    received_data = await output_queue.get()
    assert received_data == b'test_data'
```

### Backward Compatibility
- Existing `VoiceTyping` class continues to work unchanged
- New `PipelineVoiceTyping` provides pipeline-based alternative
- All existing tests pass without modification

## 📈 Benefits

### Modularity
- Each stage can be developed, tested, and maintained independently
- Easy to swap implementations (different audio sources, recognition engines)
- Clear separation of concerns

### Testability
- Stages can be unit tested in isolation using mocks
- Complex integration scenarios can be tested independently
- Better error isolation and debugging

### Extensibility
- New stages can be added without modifying existing ones
- Multiple recognition engines can run in parallel
- Performance monitoring and metrics can be added per-stage

## 🚀 Usage

### Drop-in Replacement
```python
# Use new pipeline system
voice_typing = PipelineVoiceTyping(config, state_ref, tray_manager)
voice_typing.voice_typing_loop()  # Same interface, pipeline implementation
```

### Direct Pipeline Control
```python
coordinator = AudioPipelineCoordinator(audio_input, recognition_source, callback)
await coordinator.initialize(config)
await coordinator.start_pipeline()
# Pipeline stages now communicate via queues
```

## 📊 Results

**✅ All Acceptance Criteria Met:**
- ✅ Each audio pipeline stage is modular and testable in isolation
- ✅ Data transfer between stages via queues/events, not direct calls  
- ✅ At least one end-to-end pipeline test (actually 5 comprehensive tests)

**📈 Test Coverage:**
- 9 new pipeline-specific tests
- All 58 existing tests continue to pass
- Integration tests validate system compatibility

This implementation provides a solid foundation for future enhancements while maintaining full backward compatibility and significantly improving code modularity and testability.

Fixes #39.

body:
This pull request introduces significant architectural changes, transitioning the backend routing and middleware system from `hono` to `orpc`. It also updates dependencies, simplifies authentication, and refactors providers and utilities to align with the new framework. The most important changes are grouped by theme below.

### Backend Framework Transition

* Removed `hono`-based routing and middleware, including files like `src/app/api/[[...route]]/route.ts`, `src/lib/create-app.ts`, and `src/lib/routes.ts`. These were replaced with `orpc`-based routing and middleware for better scalability and integration. ([src/app/api/[[...route]]/route.tsL1-L47](diffhunk://#diff-087a4afc4f41c98907de10383d7019c624a5216fdf90a1496a3cef40fb87227dL1-L47), [[1]](diffhunk://#diff-cb778a2b9d7fa6bca82a11965adee421938a4ed2f0600a74e0ced41b9086865bL1-L27) [[2]](diffhunk://#diff-71bb8d8c0ac95a1511071455393d02c0d5eed0cc2f7bfceadbfb78e832a6e256L1-L11)
* Introduced `orpc` utilities, such as `src/utils/orpc/orpc.middleware.ts`, `src/utils/orpc/orpc.procedure.ts`, and `src/utils/orpc/orpc.server.ts`, to handle middleware, procedures, and server-side router initialization. [[1]](diffhunk://#diff-658420125ab19bdf09ca4c03e5d194e584e63f3bcdeee8ab9e3847b8c65eb5fbR1-R59) [[2]](diffhunk://#diff-0c3e12e5a0a700bfbb15d0a5e6b7c74521826b94a0a112758abb01441e1f7083R1-R12) [[3]](diffhunk://#diff-a88f7cbd22ae5ad67eaf33673c891f5f38d19bc426d0c3c0934cc2c0fcb9672aR1-R24)

### Dependency Updates

* Updated `package.json` to remove `hono`-related dependencies and add `orpc` packages (`@orpc/client`, `@orpc/server`, `@orpc/tanstack-query`). Other dependencies were updated, such as `next-themes` and `sonner`. [[1]](diffhunk://#diff-7ae45ad102eab3b6d7e7896acd08c427a9b25b346470d7bc6507b6481575d519L24-L28) [[2]](diffhunk://#diff-7ae45ad102eab3b6d7e7896acd08c427a9b25b346470d7bc6507b6481575d519L38-R46) [[3]](diffhunk://#diff-7ae45ad102eab3b6d7e7896acd08c427a9b25b346470d7bc6507b6481575d519R55)

### Authentication Simplification

* Removed `hono`-based authentication middleware (`src/auth/auth-middleware.ts`) and replaced it with `better-auth` integration using `orpc` middleware. Simplified the authentication configuration by commenting out unused social providers. [[1]](diffhunk://#diff-5a1620a93d808086d4b45cce37e7b9b2033fd833116e476b33c984c5a487e1bcL1-L18) [[2]](diffhunk://#diff-26c98c2ffc5924a448f8384c10793435c826bb2783eff1d4f866784c95575be5L22-R25)

### Provider Refactoring

* Replaced the `ThemeProvider` with a new `Providers` component in `src/app/layout.tsx`. The new component integrates `ReactQueryDevtools`, `Toaster`, and `QueryClientProvider`. [[1]](diffhunk://#diff-29d0a55f5ca1a9951042587f8b891bb4cd8b204f5bc855dc2468ed44cde2f5b3L4-R5) [[2]](diffhunk://#diff-29d0a55f5ca1a9951042587f8b891bb4cd8b204f5bc855dc2468ed44cde2f5b3L21-R22) [[3]](diffhunk://#diff-6162b530f2f23a595c013b4c5f1be2d03365972f5bd70aad5e84f9c6394e7d8dR1-R26)

### UI Enhancements

* Added a new `Toaster` component in `src/components/ui/sonner.tsx` for displaying toast notifications, with theme integration and customizable options.

# Summary
This pull request refactors the NixOS configuration structure to improve modularity, maintainability, and clarity. The primary goal is to create a more organized and scalable configuration by separating concerns and introducing a shared library for common settings. Additionally, initial documentation has been created to guide future development and usage.

## Key changes include:
- Restructured Modules: Modules have been reorganized into nixos, darwin, and shared directories to better distinguish between OS-specific and common configurations.
- Shared Library: A new lib directory has been introduced to house shared functions and utilities, reducing code duplication.
- Configuration Migration: Existing configurations have been migrated to the new structure, ensuring a successful build on both NixOS and Darwin systems.
- Documentation: New documentation setup using NDG.

## What This PR Does
This PR adds an incremental analysis system to the codebase understanding toolkit, enabling intelligent caching of file analysis results to improve performance on large repositories. The system uses multiple invalidation strategies (mtime, file size, content hash) to determine when files need re-analysis.

## Key Changes
- **New `FileAnalysisCache` class** in `incremental_analyzer.py` that manages file-level caching with sophisticated change detection
- **Enhanced `Repository` class** with incremental symbol extraction capabilities and cache management methods
- **New `cache` CLI command** for managing the analysis cache (status, cleanup, clear, stats operations)
- **Version bump** from 1.0.3 to 1.1.0 reflecting the new incremental analysis feature
- **Cache persistence** using JSON files stored in `.kit/cache/` directory

## Impact
- **Performance improvement** for repeated analysis of large codebases through intelligent caching
- **New dependency** on cache directory structure (`.kit/cache/`) in repositories
- **Backward compatible** - existing functionality unchanged, incremental features are additive
- **CLI expansion** with new cache management commands for users to monitor and control caching behavior

author: jgrubb
body:
## Summary
- Replace '/' with '_' in AWS CUR column names instead of removing prefixes entirely
- Add consistent column cleaning logic for both CSV and parquet files
- Add comprehensive CUR v2 test coverage for dataFiles vs reportKeys behavior
- Fix test runner to use python3 instead of python

## Problem
The previous column cleaning logic was removing AWS CUR category prefixes entirely:
- `"lineItem/UnblendedCost"` → `"UnblendedCost"` ❌
- `"reservation/UnblendedCost"` → `"UnblendedCost"` ❌ (collision\!)

This caused:
1. **Column name collisions** between different categories
2. **Loss of important context** about data categorization  
3. **FOCUS compatibility issues** for future transformations

## Solution

author: aazuspan
body:
#61 relied on a specific EEException message to validate years, which wasn't being thrown by LCMS and CCAP due to their custom loading function. It's safer to catch *any* exception during `sankify` and validate years then. This could cause a false positive if you encounter a different error while using an unlisted year, but I think that's an unlikely risk that's outweighed by the benefit of reliably catching errors related to missing years.

This also separates the fetching of a given year image from the processing of that image so that Dataset subclasses don't need to duplicate processing, like setting visualization properties. Previously that wasn't being done consistently for LCMS and CCAP. In the process of making those methods more consistent, I removed some properties that were being manually set to speed things up slightly. I don't think those should be required for any reason.

author: azu
body:
## Overview

Implements a new Secretlint rule to detect Anthropic Claude API keys and integrates it with the canary preset.

## 🔍 Implementation

### New Rule: @secretlint/secretlint-rule-anthropic

- **Target**: Anthropic Claude API keys
- **Pattern**: `sk-ant-api0\d-[A-Za-z0-9_-]{90,128}AA`
- **Example**: `sk-ant-api03-z0zjHHXo5uibD2havvfqiZYJe9ENlwI1trcQC5pyDC2N2w6nbpUitUU_iR4kkSszVyUpINaxvCtun3_Mub0O3w-48GXRgAA`

### 📋 Pattern Design

Based on official documentation and real key format analysis:

- **Prefix**: `sk-ant-api0[3-4]-` (13 chars) - Official Anthropic format
- **Body**: Base64-like string 90-128 chars - Flexible range for actual key length variations
- **Suffix**: `AA` - Characteristic ending of Anthropic keys
- **Boundary**: Word boundary handling to prevent false positives

**References**:
- [Anthropic API Documentation](https://docs.anthropic.com/en/api/overview)
- [Anthropic Admin API Keys](https://docs.anthropic.com/en/api/admin-api/apikeys/get-api-key)
- [GitGuardian Claude Detection](https://docs.gitguardian.com/secrets-detection/secrets-detection-engine/detectors/specifics/claude_api_key)

## 🧪 Test Results

### Individual Rule Tests
```bash
✓ secretlint-rule-anthropic ng.secret (1.56ms)
✓ secretlint-rule-anthropic ok.valid (1.80ms)
Total: 5/5 tests passed
```

### Canary Preset Tests  
```bash
✓ All 56 tests passed including new Anthropic rule
✓ Integration with existing rules verified
✓ No conflicts or performance issues
```

### False Positive Tests
Confirmed the following patterns are correctly excluded:
- ❌ `ssk-ant-api04-...` (typo with double 's')
- ❌ `sk-ant-api02-...` / `sk-ant-api05-...` (unsupported versions)
- ❌ `sk-openai-...` (different service)
- ❌ Keys with inappropriate length (too short/too long)

## 🌐 Multi-language Support

- **English**: `found Anthropic Claude API key: {KEY}`
- **Japanese**: `Anthropic Claude API キー: {KEY} がみつかりました`

## 📁 Changed Files

```
packages/@secretlint/secretlint-rule-anthropic/
├── package.json          # New package definition
├── README.md             # Detailed usage and documentation
├── src/index.ts          # Main rule implementation
└── test/
    ├── index.test.ts     # Comprehensive test cases
    └── snapshots/        # Test snapshots

packages/@secretlint/secretlint-rule-preset-canary/
├── package.json          # Added devDependencies
├── src/index.ts          # Import and register rule
└── test/snapshots/       # Updated snapshots
    └── secretlint-rule-anthropic/  # New additions
```

## 🔄 Integration Process

### ✅ Completed
1. ✅ Created and implemented new rule package
2. ✅ Researched and implemented accurate detection pattern
3. ✅ Created comprehensive test cases
4. ✅ Multi-language support (English/Japanese)
5. ✅ **Complete integration with canary preset**
6. ✅ All tests passing (56/56)
7. ✅ Detailed documentation
8. ✅ Minimized false positives

### 🚀 Future Plan
This PR completes **canary preset integration**. Addition to **recommended preset** will be done after careful consideration in the next major version:

## 🔗 Related Issue

**Major version planning**: [Issue #1073 - Add new rules to recommended preset for v11.0.0](https://github.com/secretlint/secretlint/issues/1073)

- **Target Version**: v11.0.0
- **Breaking Change**: Potential increase in detections with new rules
- **Preparation Period**: Long-term stability confirmation in canary preset

## 🧪 Verification Commands

```bash
# Individual rule test
cd packages/@secretlint/secretlint-rule-anthropic && npm test

# Canary preset test (integration check)
cd packages/@secretlint/secretlint-rule-preset-canary && npm test

# Full project test
npm test
```

## 💡 Usage

### Standalone
```json
{
  "rules": [
    {
      "id": "@secretlint/secretlint-rule-anthropic"
    }
  ]
}
```

### With Canary Preset (available with this PR)
```json
{
  "rules": [
    {
      "id": "@secretlint/secretlint-rule-preset-canary"
    }
  ]
}
```

## 🛡️ Security Improvements

This rule mitigates the following security risks:
- Prevents accidental commits of Anthropic Claude API keys
- Reduces risk of credential leakage
- Improves security awareness across development teams

---

**Note**: This PR targets integration up to the canary preset. Addition to the recommended preset is managed in [Issue #1073](https://github.com/secretlint/secretlint/issues/1073) and will be implemented during major version updates.

body: This PR fixes the missing Open Graph meta tags and JSON-LD structured data that were preventing proper SEO and social sharing functionality on Google, LinkedIn, WhatsApp, and other platforms. ## Problem The issue was caused by Next.js 13+ Link component compatibility problems. The codebase was using the legacy Link syntax with nested `` tags: ```jsx Blog ``` This caused server-side rendering failures, preventing the SEO component from properly generating metadata during static site generation. ## Solution Updated all Link components to use the modern Next.js 13+ syntax: ```jsx Blog ``` ## Changes Made - **`pages/index.js`**: Fixed Link component for blog navigation - **`pages/blog/index.js`**: Fixed Link component for home navigation - **`pages/blog/[slug].js`**: Fixed Link component for blog navigation - **`components/BlogPostPreview.js`**: Fixed Link component for post titles ## Validation All pages now correctly render complete metadata: ✅ **Homepage**: OG meta, Twitter cards, canonical URL, robots meta ✅ **Blog Index**: OG meta, Twitter cards, canonical URL, robots meta ✅ **Blog Posts**: OG meta, Twitter cards, article metadata, JSON-LD structured data, canonical URL, robots meta The static export now generates fully pre-rendered HTML with all metadata properly baked in, ensuring social sharing previews work correctly across all platforms. Fixes #38. --- 💬 Share your feedback on Copilot coding agent for the chance to win a $200 gift card! Click [here](https://survey.alchemer.com/s3/8343779/Copilot-Coding-agent) to start the survey.

author: charlvs
body:
Implement a comprehensive seed node configuration system that fetches
seed nodes from the Komodo Platform repository with automatic fallback
to hardcoded defaults.

### New Features:
- Add SeedNode and SeedNodeContact types for type-safe configuration
- Implement SeedNodeUpdater for fetching remote seed nodes
- Add SeedNodeService with automatic fallback mechanism
- Add SeedNodeValidator with enhanced P2P configuration validation
- Export seed node service from komodo_defi_framework

### Configuration Updates:
- Update build_config.json to include seed-nodes.json mapping
- Add seed_nodes.json to gitignore for dynamic assets
- Change API branch from 'dev' to 'alt-main'
- Update all platform binary checksums and commit hashes

### Framework Integration:
- Add automatic seed node fetching to KdfStartupConfig
- Integrate SeedNodeService into auth service for wallet creation
- Fix trading protocol parameter name (trading_proto_v2 -> use_trading_proto_v2)
- Improve boolean validation in SeedNodeValidator

### Documentation:
- Add comprehensive SEED_NODES_GUIDE.md with usage examples
- Include example code for seed node functionality
- Add complete test coverage for new types and services

### Dependencies:
- Add komodo_coin_updates dependency to komodo_defi_framework
- Export seed node types from komodo_defi_types
- Update pubspec.lock files across packages

The seed node system ensures applications always have access to current
seed nodes while maintaining backwards compatibility through fallback
mechanisms. This addresses the upcoming requirement in v2.5.0-beta
where seed nodes will be mandatory unless P2P is disabled.

Breaking changes: None - all changes are additive with sensible defaults.

body:
This pull request introduces several enhancements and fixes across multiple components, focusing on improved functionality, user experience, and code consistency. Key changes include updates to image handling, integration of animations for smoother user interactions, and adjustments to component props and behavior. Below is a categorized summary of the most important changes:

### Image Handling Enhancements:
* Added support for dynamic user profile pictures in `Avatar`, using the `useGetProfile` hook and default fallback images based on gender. Updated `Avatar` props to include `size` as a number instead of a string. (`src/components/Avatar.tsx`, [src/components/Avatar.tsxR1-R46](diffhunk://#diff-244cdd9be92eb59eaa9aa7b7d3e310ab0b3845111e3de28746ec3ea59ae970b4R1-R46))
* Introduced a new `FormImageDropzone` component for image uploads, with drag-and-drop functionality and progress tracking. (`src/components/forms/FormImageDropzone.tsx`, [src/components/forms/FormImageDropzone.tsxR1-R130](diffhunk://#diff-b068149183fc7e0654757c72f963f83432f5437884679805ec0f0b9e7bba957dR1-R130))

### Animation Integration:
* Incorporated `framer-motion` animations for smoother transitions in `AnimatedButton`, `VideoTile`, `CommentItem`, and `PostBody`. These changes enhance user experience with hover effects, entry/exit animations, and spring-based transitions. (`src/components/agora/AnimatedButton.tsx`, [[1]](diffhunk://#diff-80bceeeb39f0bea2312fb9ef9b5756b1172fe7d3f8a49d50229bc039819b5d36R21-R48); `src/components/agora/VideoTile.tsx`, [[2]](diffhunk://#diff-c64ba20f371fa69e5370de2fd0db6a8fd8e4d2d0afceac5b9d437579f50af7e3L49-R51) [[3]](diffhunk://#diff-c64ba20f371fa69e5370de2fd0db6a8fd8e4d2d0afceac5b9d437579f50af7e3L67-R67); `src/components/posts/comments/CommentItem.tsx`, [[4]](diffhunk://#diff-c6f788daf3876216e88f53f0f065f57d807a95a2a96ad5c21d047fbb23f8d044L16-R48); `src/components/posts/posts/PostBody.tsx`, [[5]](diffhunk://#diff-0c65ce100866f864885626eec1355836f3ab2ff86a764cb6c511a4f094e79e89R38-R61)

### Component Updates:

### Code Consistency and Fixes:
* Adjusted `FormDropzone` dependencies in `useEffect` to include `res` and `onChange` for proper reactivity. (`src/components/forms/FormDropzone.tsx`, [src/components/forms/FormDropzone.tsxL101-R103](diffhunk://#diff-d36d23edb8241bc67764fe1a81df109684350b7055384e67b3bc5a1511c680bfL101-R103))

author: rahulkushwaha
body:
This is a little different from the embedded innodb. Here we are creating a loop using tokio async, and checking for `n` number of messages or deadline. If either one of them is crossed, we trigger log write.
- Implement LogFlusherLoop that houses the infinite loop to write to disk and fetch more.
- The trigger for more logs is a mpsc queue that accepts LogTrigger messages.
- The message can also be a poison pill that stop the loop.
- `LogFlushNotifier` is used to recive notification for loop events. Helps in testings for now.
